text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. In supervised learning, the most common type, we give the computer a set of training data. This data includes examples with known answers, like photos labeled "cat" or "dog." The computer uses these examples to build a model, which is like a rule or pattern it discovers. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data—for instance, identifying a new photo as a cat. We measure how well the model works by its accuracy, which tells us the percentage of correct predictions.
